The publications site linked by Trier lists the H-Soz-Kult review of Susanne Ruf's Die Stiftungen der Familie Hardenrath.
The 19 February 2014 review of Ruf's book is by Wolfgang Schmid, Department III – History, University of Trier.

basis: Trier's publications page attributes a book on side a to its Wolfgang Schmid and links to the publications site listing the review on side b. H-Soz-Kult independently identifies the reviewer with Trier's history department in 2014.

evidence.says: Posts and Pasts: A Theory of Postcolonialism names Alfred J. López as its author.
Oxford identifies Alfred J. López with the Department of English at Purdue University.

basis: The AHA record identifies the 1996 St. Rose of Lima dissertation with the University of New Mexico, but the sources found do not link its author to the author of Posts and Pasts. The shared name is insufficient to establish identity or a difference.

evidence.says: Létourneau lists Frédéric Demers's 1998 Céline Dion master's thesis and his 2004 doctoral thesis on Les Filles de Caleb.
The Laval thesis catalogue lists Demers's Céline Dion thesis in 1998 and his Les Filles de Caleb thesis in 2005.
Frédéric Demers's 2002 article on Les Filles de Caleb cites his 1999 book Céline Dion et l'identité québécoise.

basis: The supervisor's CV and Laval catalogue connect the Céline Dion research and a doctoral thesis on Les Filles de Caleb to Frédéric Demers; his 2002 article also cites the book. The catalogue gives the doctoral thesis a different title from the AHA record, so the identification of that thesis with the AHA entry is inferred.

evidence.says: The publisher credits Lindsey Dodd with Feeling Memory and identifies her as author of French Children Under the Allied Bombs, 1940–1945: An Oral History (2016).

basis: The publisher identifies the author of the book on side a as the author of the 2016 work on side b.

evidence.says: Taisu Zhang's dissertation is titled Kinship, Property, and Agricultural Capitalism in Pre-Industrial China and England.
Zhang's book The Laws and Economics of Confucianism was recognized in dissertation form; he received a Yale history Ph.D. in 2014.
Yale lists Taisu Zhang as author of The Ideological Foundations of Qing Taxation and The Laws and Economics of Confucianism.

basis: Duke names the dissertation on key b, while Yale lists the book on key a and the book developed from that dissertation under the same scholar. The National Committee profile identifies the latter book in dissertation form.

evidence.says: The author of Timber and Forestry in Qing China earned a history PhD at UCLA in 2017 and was at Vanderbilt.
The author of From respirator to Wu’s mask earned a history PhD at Peking University in 2018.
Meng Zhang at Manchester has ORCID 0000-0002-1899-9110 and trained in history at Peking University.

basis: The book author and the mask article author have different history doctorates and careers. The Manchester profile links the latter to b's ORCID; b may also contain unrelated works.

evidence.says: The 2019 article lists Selma Leydesdorff, ORCID 0000-0003-2691-9480, as professor of oral history and culture at the University of Amsterdam.
The author biography identifies Selma Leydesdorff as professor emerita of oral history and culture at Amsterdam and lists Surviving the Bosnian Genocide among her publications.

basis: The article identifies the ORCID-bearing author as the University of Amsterdam professor of oral history and culture. The publisher preview identifies the same professor as author of the book on the other key.

evidence.says: Lukas Engelmann's publications include Ein queeres Bild von AIDS (2012) and Krankheitsbild AIDS (2013).
Is This the End? The Eclipse of the Therapeutic Revolution was held at the University of Zurich on 4–6 October 2012.
Lukas Engelmann received his PhD at Humboldt University in 2013 and became a research fellow at the University of Zurich in April 2013.

basis: The conference report could not be independently linked to the author of the works on the first key. The conference's Zurich location alone does not establish the reviewer's institutional affiliation, and the documented Zurich fellowship began after the report.

evidence.says: Kent State lists Kathleen Endres's dissertation The Power of the Tradition, The Potential for Change: The Women of Cleveland, 1850-1890 under 1985.
Kathleen L. Endres, associate professor of communication at Akron, earned her Ph.D. at Kent State University in 1985.
The review identifies Akron communications professor Kathleen Endres as the author of Rosie the Rubber Worker and Akron's Better Half.

basis: The dissertation is listed at Kent State in 1985, the same institution and year as the doctorate of the Akron professor identified as the author of books on the other key. This is a strong institutional and chronological link.

evidence.says: Kristin Poling wrote Germany’s Urban Frontiers and was a visiting assistant professor at the University of Rochester in 2012–2014.
Kristin Poling’s CV lists her October 2014 H-Net review of Jens Lachmund’s Greening Berlin.

basis: The university promotion record links the author of the book on key a to Rochester during the review period. Poling’s CV independently lists the review on key b.

evidence.says: Jonas Brendebach of the European University Institute wrote the 2014 report on Ideologies of Empire and organized a 2016 conference with Martin Herzer and Heidi Tworek.
Jonas Brendebach, Martin Herzer and Heidi Tworek edited International Organizations and the Media (2018); Brendebach was a European University Institute researcher.

basis: The 2014 report and the book editor are associated with the European University Institute in the same career period. The report author's conference collaborators are also the book's coeditors, providing a further career link.
